sources.title: Urban building energy modeling – A review of a nascent field
sources.citation_apa: Reinhart, C. F., & Cerezo Davila, C. (2016). Urban building energy modeling – A review of a nascent field. Building and Environment, 97, 196–202. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.buildenv.2015.12.001
sources.source_type: Peer-reviewed methods review; original article text read via secondary host; metadata checked against MIT repository.

method_facts.fact: UBEM combines climate, geometry, construction standards and use schedules; archetypes group buildings and then assign thermal properties.
The workflow separates input organization, thermal model generation/execution and validation.

inputs_stated: Weather; envelope geometry and window ratios; terrain; constructions; HVAC systems; use schedules.
outputs_stated: Operational building load profiles, presented spatially and temporally.

source_limitations.text: Individual-building errors can exceed aggregate errors; limited audited and metered data constrain archetype calibration.

sources.studio_role_inference: A framework for district building-energy and retrofit scenarios, with validation matched to the decision scale.
sources.verification: Metadata and quoted sections checked; no original validation case reanalysis.

sources.title: Deriving the operational procedure for the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI)
sources.citation_apa: Bröde, P., Fiala, D., Błażejczyk, K., Holmér, I., Jendritzky, G., Kampmann, B., Tinz, B., & Havenith, G. (2012). Deriving the operational procedure for the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI). International Journal of Biometeorology, 56, 481–494. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00484-011-0454-1

method_facts.fact: UTCI is the reference-environment air temperature producing an equivalent modeled dynamic physiological response.
The procedure combines the UTCI-Fiala thermoregulation model with adaptive clothing and provides thermal-stress categories and fast calculation approximations.

inputs_stated: Wind speed; radiation; humidity; air temperature.
outputs_stated: UTCI equivalent temperature and thermal-stress category.
sources.studio_role_inference: Defines a human-exposure outcome connecting radiation/shade and wind to outdoor thermal assessment.
sources.verification: Publisher title, all authors, DOI, online date and issue date verified; full methods and numerical validity bounds not read.

sources.title: 12.2. SOLWEIG Manual
sources.publication_year_note: Living manual, accessed 2026-10-18. Lists stable v2025a released 2 May 2025 and development v2026a.
sources.citation_apa: UMEP/SOLWEIG development team. (n.d.). SOLWEIG manual. UMEP Manual. Retrieved October 18, 2026, from https://umep-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/OtherManuals/SOLWEIG.html

method_facts.fact: SOLWEIG computes directional shortwave and longwave radiation to estimate mean radiant temperature.
Surface grids need common extent, resolution and CRS; wind forcing is required for PET/UTCI at points of interest.

inputs_stated: Building/ground DSM; optional canopy/trunk DSMs; DEM or building land-cover grid; weather, location, albedo/emissivity and human exposure settings.
outputs_stated: Mean radiant temperature, radiation and shadow grids; point time series including PET and UTCI.

source_limitations.text: The documented older ground scheme evaluates grass and impervious surfaces; water and bare soil are first-order approximations. The manual discourages interpreting building-roof fluxes.

sources.studio_role_inference: Provides a reproducible shade and pedestrian radiant-exposure path linked to GIS geometry.
sources.verification: Official manual sections read; versions distinguished; no model run or performance claim.

sources.title: AIJ guidelines for practical applications of CFD to pedestrian wind environment around buildings
sources.citation_apa: Tominaga, Y., Mochida, A., Yoshie, R., Kataoka, H., Nozu, T., Yoshikawa, M., & Shirasawa, T. (2008). AIJ guidelines for practical applications of CFD to pedestrian wind environment around buildings. Journal of Wind Engineering and Industrial Aerodynamics, 96(10–11), 1749–1761. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jweia.2008.02.058
sources.source_type: Peer-reviewed technical guideline with benchmark comparisons
locators: p.1749 abstract, indexed PDF excerpt; AIJ reference [19] indexed official page

method_facts.fact: Guidelines are grounded in cross-comparisons of CFD, wind-tunnel tests and field measurements across seven test cases.

inputs_stated: CFD predictions, wind-tunnel results and field measurements for benchmark cases (study evidence inputs).
outputs_stated: Guidance for predicting pedestrian wind around buildings.
sources.studio_role_inference: A Japan-specific reference for a wind-model validation plan.
sources.verification: Title, seven authors, DOI and pages verified from indexed original-PDF opening and official AIJ reference list. Full text retrieval failed; no numeric mesh/domain prescription asserted.

sources.title: Best Practice Guideline for the CFD Simulation of Flows in the Urban Environment
sources.citation_apa: Franke, J., Hellsten, A., Schlünzen, H., & Carissimo, B. (Eds.). (2007). Best practice guideline for the CFD simulation of flows in the urban environment. COST Action 732. COST Office.

method_facts.fact: Evaluation separates physical-model uncertainty from numerical errors, including discretization and iterative convergence.
Convergence assessment monitors physical target variables as well as residuals.

inputs_stated: Geometry, inflow and other boundary conditions, initial conditions, mesh and numerical/model choices.
outputs_stated: Procedures to quantify and reduce error in urban-flow CFD.

source_limitations.text: The guideline primarily covers statistically steady RANS in neutral stratification; additional guidance is needed for non-neutral flow.

sources.studio_role_inference: Helps separate a converged wind calculation from a physically validated result, and identifies the scope gap for wind–heat coupling.
sources.verification: University of Hamburg official listing confirms document; original report text read from mirror. No universal validation threshold claimed.

sources.title: Whole life carbon assessment for the built environment
sources.publication_year_note: Second edition September 2023; retrieved Version 3 issued August 2024, effective 1 July 2024.
sources.citation_apa: Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors. (2023). Whole life carbon assessment for the built environment (2nd ed., Version 3, August 2024).

method_facts.fact: Retrofit projects report life-cycle stages over a defined study period, with module D reported separately.
Retained elements exclude previous manufacturing impacts from retrofit A1–A5, while their future maintenance and end-of-life impacts remain relevant.

inputs_stated: Retained/new element scope; product carbon data; project area; study period and future maintenance/replacement assumptions.
outputs_stated: Life-cycle carbon by module and project part, reported as total tCO2e and area intensity kgCO2e/m².

source_limitations.text: Early design product choices are uncertain; later assessments favor manufacturer-specific EPDs where available.

sources.studio_role_inference: Defines consistent carbon accounting for retention, retrofit and replacement options.
sources.verification: Official PDF downloaded and extracted on mdx1; exact edition/version and read pages checked.

sources.title: Global Protocol for Community-Scale Greenhouse Gas Emission Inventories: An Accounting and Reporting Standard for Cities, Version 1.1
sources.publication_year_note: PDF states updated June 2021; original edition 2014.
sources.citation_apa: World Resources Institute, C40 Cities Climate Leadership Group, & ICLEI – Local Governments for Sustainability. (2021). Global protocol for community-scale greenhouse gas emission inventories: An accounting and reporting standard for cities (Version 1.1).

method_facts.fact: Scopes distinguish territorial emissions, grid-supplied energy used inside the boundary, and other outside emissions caused by activities inside it.
Most sources are estimated from activity data multiplied by emission factors; GPC specifies accounting rules without imposing one calculation method.

inputs_stated: Inventory boundary; activity data; relevant emission factors.
outputs_stated: Emissions inventories in tonnes of each greenhouse gas and CO2 equivalents.
sources.limitations_assessment: No methodological weakness assessed; declared scope is city inventories.
sources.studio_role_inference: Supplies boundary discipline for a district carbon ledger; a district adaptation should state its boundary and avoid double-counting building and area totals.
sources.verification: Official landing page and PDF checked; PDF read remotely after browser size limit.

sources.title: Collaborative Governance in Theory and Practice
sources.citation_apa: Ansell, C., & Gash, A. (2008). Collaborative governance in theory and practice. Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory, 18(4), 543–571. https://doi.org/10.1093/jopart/mum032
locators: A Model of Collaborative Governance, pp.547–550; Figure 1

method_facts.fact: The model organizes starting conditions, institutional design, facilitative leadership and an iterative collaborative process.
Authors develop the model through successive comparison and refinement using 137 cases.

inputs_stated: Published case studies; stakeholder power/resources, participation incentives and prior cooperation/conflict.
outputs_stated: A contingency model of conditions associated with collaboration.

source_limitations.text: English-language coverage overrepresents American cases. Most cases evaluate process outcomes, limiting comparisons of policy effectiveness between governance modes.

sources.studio_role_inference: Structures stakeholder mapping, shared evidence discussions and decision-process documentation.
sources.verification: Original article PDF read via Oregon State mirror; journal metadata cross-checked with JSTOR; publisher fetch blocked.

sources.title: Polycentric systems for coping with collective action and global environmental change
sources.citation_apa: Ostrom, E. (2010). Polycentric systems for coping with collective action and global environmental change. Global Environmental Change, 20(4), 550–557. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gloenvcha.2010.07.004

method_facts.fact: Polycentric governance has multiple partly independent authorities across scales, linked through cooperation, monitoring and conflict resolution.
The argument emphasizes local knowledge and learning across policy experiments.

inputs_stated: Conceptual argument and examples of collective action across governance scales; no standardized numerical input set.
outputs_stated: An analytical argument for multilevel climate action and learning.

source_limitations.text: Multiple actors can create leakage, inconsistent policies, weak certification, gaming and free riding.

sources.studio_role_inference: Connects building owners, street managers, community groups and municipal action without treating fragmented authority as automatically effective.
sources.verification: Publisher metadata/abstract and original article PDF mirror checked; conceptual claims kept separate from measured effects.

verification_policy.evidence_classification: Source type and claim-level read scope, not clinical evidence ranks.
verification_policy.coi_check: Not comprehensively assessed; no claim of absence.
verification_policy.predatory_venue_check: Original publisher/institutional provenance checked; no subscription index audit performed.
verification_policy.cross_source_check: COST and AIJ overlap on benchmark validation; UBEM and RICS cover different accounting boundaries. No experimental effect size generalized.
